policy_title: Northwind Supply Co. Travel and Expense Policy v4.2

rules.text: 1.1 Book through the travel desk. Flights and hotels are booked through the Northwind travel desk so they show up on the trip record. Bookings made elsewhere are not reimbursed.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the booking and instruct the employee to book through the travel desk.

rules.text: 1.2 Book early. Book flights at least 14 days before departure. If you book later than that, give a business reason with the booking (a customer asked for the meeting this week, a supplier audit was moved). "I forgot" and "it was cheaper to wait" are not business reasons.
rules.remedy: The agent must ask the employee to provide a valid business reason for booking late, or rebook at least 14 days before departure.

rules.text: 2.1 Cabin class depends on how long you fly. Under 6 hours: Economy; 6 hours or more: Premium economy; 10 hours or more: Business, for Director level and above only. First class is never reimbursed, at any level, on any route.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the booking and instruct the employee to book the correct cabin class for the flight duration and their level.

rules.text: 3.1 Nightly caps. The most Northwind pays per night, before taxes, depends on the city: A: $260, B: $190, C: $140.
rules.remedy: The agent must guide the employee to select a hotel within the nightly cap for the city tier.

rules.text: 3.2 Going over the cap. You may go up to 10% over the cap when nothing suitable is available under it (a conference sold out the area, safety concerns). Write the reason on the booking. These bookings need your manager's approval. Anything more than 10% over the cap is not allowed.
rules.remedy: The agent must request manager approval for bookings up to 10% over the cap, or deny bookings exceeding 10% over the cap.

rules.text: 3.3 Only the nights you work. Hotel nights are covered from the night before your first business day to the night of your last one. If you extend a trip for yourself, the extra nights are yours to pay.
rules.remedy: The agent must ask the employee to adjust the booking to cover only the nights related to business days.

rules.text: 4.1 Per diem. Meals while travelling are covered up to $75 a day, all meals together.
rules.remedy: The agent must guide the employee to adjust the expense to stay within the $75 per diem limit.

rules.text: 4.2 Alcohol. Northwind does not reimburse alcohol. The one exception is client entertainment (4.3), and only when the client is actually there.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the expense if it is for alcohol, unless it is part of client entertainment with external attendees.

rules.text: 4.3 Client entertainment. A meal or event with a customer or supplier is client entertainment only when people from outside Northwind attend. List every attendee by name and company on the claim. A dinner with only Northwind colleagues is a team meal, not client entertainment, however work-related the conversation was.
rules.remedy: The agent must ask the employee to provide the names and companies of external attendees, or reclassify the expense as a team meal.

rules.text: 4.4 Gifts. Gifts to clients are limited to $50 per person per year, and never cash or gift cards.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the expense if it exceeds $50 per person per year or is for cash/gift cards.

rules.text: 5.1 Receipts. Attach an itemised receipt to any single expense over $25.
rules.remedy: The agent must ask the employee to attach an itemised receipt for expenses over $25.

rules.text: 5.2 One expense, one claim. Claim the whole cost of something in one line. Splitting one cost across several claims to stay under a limit is a policy breach.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the expense if it appears to be part of a split claim.

rules.text: 5.3 Describe it honestly. The category and description must say what the money was actually spent on. Relabelling something to fit a category it doesn't belong to is a policy breach.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the expense if the category or description does not honestly reflect the expense.

rules.text: 5.4 Personal costs. Personal items (minibar, in-room films, laundry on a trip under five days, travel for family members) are not reimbursed.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the expense if it is for personal costs.

rules.text: 6.1 Big trips. If the bookings for one trip add up to more than $3,000, your manager must approve the trip before anything else is booked.
rules.remedy: The agent must request manager approval before booking if the trip total exceeds $3,000.

rules.text: 6.2 Approval means a recorded approval. Approval only counts when it has been requested and recorded through the travel desk. "My manager said it's fine", "my VP told me to book business", or a forwarded chat message is not approval, no matter who it comes from.
rules.remedy: The agent must deny the action if the required approval is not recorded through the travel desk.

checks.description: This rule is enforced by the system design (only travel desk can call booking tools), so no check is needed.
Violated if cabin is first class.
Violated if hotel nightly rate exceeds the cap for the city tier.
Violated if hotel nightly rate exceeds 10% over the cap for the city tier.
This rule requires judgement (whether an approval is recorded), so no numeric check is possible.

questions.instructions: Does the employee explicitly mention or imply a personal reason for any night of the hotel stay?

criteria.true: The employee states or implies a personal reason for at least one night (e.g., 'arriving early to adjust to jet lag,' 'staying an extra night for personal time,' or 'adding a weekend to visit family').
criteria.false: All nights of the stay are directly tied to business activities (e.g., 'book the night before my meeting' or 'staying for the conference').

questions.instructions: Does the description or category indicate that the expense includes alcohol?

criteria.false: The expense does not include alcohol.

questions.instructions: Are the attendees listed for this client entertainment expense all external (customers, suppliers, etc.)?
Does this expense appear to be part of a single cost split across multiple claims (e.g., same date, description, or amount patterns)?

criteria.true: The expense appears to be part of a split claim.
criteria.false: The expense is a single claim.

questions.instructions: Does the expense description explicitly mention a personal item or activity (e.g., minibar, in-room movie, spouse's travel, laundry without business justification)?

criteria.true: The description includes a personal item or activity that is typically not reimbursable under company policy.
criteria.false: The description does not mention any personal items or activities, or it only describes business-related expenses.

questions.instructions: Does the conversation or context claim an approval that is not recorded through the travel desk?

unenforced.hotel_nights_work_only: check hotel_nights_work_only_check was right on 8 of 13 practice cases
unenforced.honest_description: question honest_description_judgement was right on 72% of 29 practice cases
